title: Working for God in a Godless World
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Yukito Urabe, son of a cult leader, dies when his father sacrifices him to the cult's god Mitama, praying with his last breath for a world without religion. He wakes in a faithless world and settles in a village of outcasts, but when the empire begins executing them, Mitama appears and Urabe must build a following of believers, using his father's methods, to give her power to protect them. Seinen satire and fantasy by Aoi Akashiro and Hangetsuban Sonshou; published by Titan Manga.
life_message: Belief is a powerful human tool that can manipulate or protect, and what matters is whether it is used to save people.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflict is about survival of the village rather than personal honor.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Outcasts resist an empire that purges its citizens (publisher blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Urabe protects the whole outcast village, not his own kin.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Imperial authority opposed; Urabe builds a following around himself.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Faithless world versus a newly made religion; both satirized.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Physical survival under purges drives the plot.

folkways.japan: Satirizes Japanese new-religion cults and the isekai genre; reflects a common Japanese wariness of organized religious groups.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer notes tonal swings and lack of subtlety, not preaching; religion theme carried by plot (to verify).
delivery.note: Both cult religion and the faithless empire are shown harshly, while faith itself is shown as useful.

winners_losers: Urabe and Mitama's growing following win against the empire; the cult father and the purging state lose sympathy.
